title: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
focus: Milloin asks when something happens. Milloin sinä tulet? — Tulen huomenna.
targetSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “When are you coming?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. Milloin asks when something happens. Put it before the supplied clause: Milloin sinä tulet? (“When are you coming?”). Present-tense Finnish can describe a planned future event when a time word makes the meaning clear. The complete question means “When are you coming”.
requiredSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
exercises.targetSkill: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions

parts.formation: Milloin asks for the time of an event.

optionFeedback.Milloin sinä tulet?: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. Milloin asks when something happens. optionFeedback.Missä sinä tulet?: Missä asks for a location: where. The requested question is “Milloin sinä tulet?”

exercises.prompt: Answer “Milloin te menette?”: choose “We are going in the morning.”
exercises.explanation: Answer with a time expression such as tänään (“today”), huomenna (“tomorrow”), nyt (“now”), aamulla (“in the morning”) or illalla (“in the evening”). These taught expressions are learned as complete forms. A full reply includes the appropriate verb; a short time expression also answers milloin. The complete reply means “We are going in the morning”.
